summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with right-sided neck and head pain, transient vision loss, and ear drainage, following a recent diagnosis of classical Hodgkin lymphoma. Imaging revealed a rapidly enlarging nasopharyngeal mass with skull base and nerve involvement, explaining her symptoms. She received ICE chemotherapy and intrathecal methotrexate, with a lumbar puncture performed for CNS evaluation. During admission, she developed neutropenic fever, managed with cefepime, and mucositis, complicated by a methadone-fluconazole interaction, leading to a switch to micafungin. Her diabetes required insulin due to steroid-induced hyperglycemia, and she received a blood transfusion for symptomatic microcytic anemia. IVIG was administered for immunodeficiency. Her pain improved with optimized analgesia, including increased pregabalin. She stabilized, completed treatment, and was discharged home with follow-up in oncology, neuro-ophthalmology, and immunology.
